To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cRGD inhibits monocyte infiltration of the vascular endothelum, which is associated with reduced macrophage infiltration into the vascular wall.

the cyclic peptide cRGD inhibited the infiltration of the injured vasculature and the renal microvascule by monocytes/macrophages and the lipid accumulation in these tissues, but did not affect formation of fatty streaks.
a cRGD peptide inhibits macrovascular and microvascular monocyte/macrophages infiltration, and lipid accumulation in a model of atherosclerosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the role of VLA4 in the pathogenesis and progression of vascular disease.
the development of novel antiatherosclerotic strategies based on inhibition of leukocyte adhesion to the vascular endothelum.
the development of novel anti-inflammatory agents that can be useful in the treatment of inflammatory disorders, including atherosclerotic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition of VLA4-vascular cell adhesion molecules interactions with cRGD is a promising strategy for the treatment of atherogenesis and renal disease.
cRGD is a potent inhibitor in vivo of macrophage infiltration, but not of lipid accumulation.
cRGD is a potent inhibitor in vivo of monocyte/macropage adhesion to the endothelium and infiltration of the microvasculature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cRGD inhibits macrophages from entering the vascular wall and that this effect is mediated through the very late antigen 4 receptor.
the cRGD peptide, which inhibits the adhesion of leukocytes to the vascular endothelum in vitro, inhibits their infiltration into the injured vascular wall and the kidney.
cRGD is an inhibitor of monocyte infiltration and lipid deposition in injured vasculature but not in atherogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the VLA4 pathway may be involved in the recruitment of monocytes/macrophages in the injured macrovascualture, but not in the development of fatty streaks, and therefore may be a potential therapeutic target in atherosclerosis.
cRGD treatment of ApoE-/--mice resulted in the attenuation of macrophage infiltration into the injured vasculature and in the reduction of lipid accumulation in the kidney and the carotid arteries.
the inhibition of the VLA-4/VCAM-1 interaction may not be a sufficient strategy to inhibit atherogenesis in vivo.
